slides.title: Mapping the Network, Not Just the Names
bullets: Basic mapping identifies who the influential experts are
Advanced mapping visualises how experts relate to and influence one another
Strategy then accounts for the network, not isolated individuals

slides.title: Relationships Are the Real Content
bullets: Identifies, profiles and visualises experts and influence networks
Captures who trains under whom and who co-authors with whom
Tracks shared committees and who amplifies whose digital content
Notes which regional experts defer scientifically to national ones

slides.title: Three Practical Payoffs of Network Mapping
bullets: Reveals indirect influence through a central network position
Clarifies where real consensus exists versus real disagreement
Shows likely cascade effects when a Tier 1 opinion shifts

slides.title: What Advanced Mapping Draws On
bullets: Bibliometric and citation data
Congress and society participation records
Clinical trial investigator databases
Digital engagement data covering the DOL dimension

slides.title: Field Intelligence No Database Provides
bullets: Knowing who a KOL actually trusts and listens to
Spotting rising credibility before it shows up in publication metrics
Recognising when a senior name has limited real prescribing influence
Mapping works best as structured data plus genuine field knowledge

takeaway.title: Advanced mapping visualises how KOLs influence each other, not just who they are
bullets: Network position can matter as much as individual recognition
Multiple data sources combine with real field intelligence
Mapping reveals cascade effects when a top-tier opinion shifts
